objects.description: Protocol Buffers generated enum representing error/status codes for the interactive subsystem. Values cover common success/failure categories and service-specific errors. Utility functions for validation, name lookup, and parsing are provided by protobuf.

Lightweight status object encapsulating an error code (StatusCode, alias of gs::flex::interactive::Code) and an optional message. Provides constructors for code/message, ok() predicate, accessors, and ToString. Default constructs to an unspecified state per implementation; OK() returns a success status.
Type alias mapping gs::StatusCode to the protobuf-generated enum gs::flex::interactive::Code for error/status codes.

functions.name: gs::flex::interactive::Code_IsValid
functions.description: Checks whether the provided integer corresponds to a valid gs::flex::interactive::Code enum value. Useful before casting integers to the enum.
requirements: value may be any int; returns true if it maps to a defined Code, false otherwise

functions.name: gs::flex::interactive::Code_descriptor
functions.description: Returns the protobuf EnumDescriptor for gs::flex::interactive::Code, enabling reflection-based operations (e.g., listing names/values).
requirements: May return a non-null descriptor pointer managed by protobuf; caller must not delete it

functions.name: gs::flex::interactive::Code_Name
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline const std::string& gs::flex::interactive::Code_Name(T enum_t_value);
functions.description: Returns the enum constant name string for the given Code value (or integral equivalent). Uses protobuf internal NameOfEnum. If the value is not a defined enumerator, the resulting name is implementation-defined by protobuf.
requirements: Template parameter T must be gs::flex::interactive::Code or an integral type (enforced by static_assert)
enum_t_value should represent a valid Code value to obtain a meaningful name
Returned reference remains valid as provided by protobuf internals; treat as read-only

functions.name: gs::flex::interactive::Code_Parse
functions.signature: inline bool gs::flex::interactive::Code_Parse(const std::string& name, gs::flex::interactive::Code* value);
functions.description: Parses an enum name into a gs::flex::interactive::Code value. Returns true on success and writes the parsed value to value.
requirements: value must be a non-null pointer to receive the parsed enum
name should match an existing enumerator name exactly as defined in the descriptor to succeed
On failure, the function returns false and does not set a valid Code

functions.name: gs::Status::ok
functions.description: Returns true if the Status represents success (OK).

functions.name: gs::Status::error_message
functions.description: Returns the stored error message string. For OK status, this may be empty.

functions.name: gs::Status::OK
functions.description: Creates and returns a Status representing success (OK).

functions.name: gs::Status::ToString
functions.description: Returns a string representation of the status, typically including the code and message. Exact format is defined by the implementation.

functions.name: std::to_string
functions.description: Formats a gs::flex::interactive::Code value as a string in the form "05-XXXX" where XXXX is a zero-padded 4-digit decimal of the code.
requirements: status may be any Code value; function never throws based on header content provided

data_types.description: A textual representation of an enumeration constant’s name as defined in code or a schema (e.g., protobuf EnumDescriptor). The string must exactly match one of the enumerator identifiers (case-sensitive, no extra whitespace) for parsing functions like Code_Parse to succeed. Arbitrary strings may fail to parse.

import random
from typing import List

enum_names: List[bytes] = [
    b"OK",
    b"CANCELLED",
    b"INVALID_ARGUMENT",
    b"TIMEOUT",
    b"NOT_FOUND",
    b"ALREADY_EXISTS",
    b"RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED",
    b"UNIMPLEMENTED",
    b"PERMISSION_DENIED",
    b"COMPILATION_FAILURE",
    b"PORT_IN_USE",
    b"UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION",
    b"ILLEGAL_STATE",
    b"NETWORK_FAILURE",
    b"BAD_REQUEST",
    b"SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE",
    b"CODEGEN_ERROR",
    b"INVALID_SCHEMA",
    b"ILLEGAL_OPERATION",
    b"INTERNAL_ERROR",
    b"INVALID_IMPORT_FILE",
    b"IO_ERROR",
    b"QUERY_FAILED",
    b"REOPEN_ERROR",
    b"ERROR_OPEN_META",
    b"SQL_EXECUTION_ERROR",
    b"SQL_BINDING_ERROR",
    b"ALREADY_LOCKED",
    b"UNKNOWN",
]

# Additional interesting non-matching strings to exercise failure paths
non_matching: List[bytes] = [
    b"ok",                     # case mismatch
    b" OK",                    # leading space
    b"OK ",                    # trailing space
    b"PERMISSION- DENIED",     # punctuation/space
    b"PERMISSION_DENlED",      # looks similar (small L instead of I)
    b"NOT__FOUND",             # extra underscore
    b"TIME OUT",               # space in between
    b"INVALID-ARGUMENT",
    b"unknown",
    b"",                        # empty
    b"CODE_100",               # numeric-like but invalid
    b"SERVICE-UNAVAILABLE",
    b"PORT-IN-USE",
    b"ALREADY-EXISTS",
]

# Some valid aliases that protobuf often accepts via reflection only if names match exactly
# We keep only exact names in enum_names; anything else should generally fail.


def _weighted_choice(rng: random.Random, items):
    total = sum(w for w, _ in items)
    x = rng.uniform(0, total)
    upto = 0.0
    for w, v in items:
        if upto + w >= x:
            return v
        upto += w
    return items[-1][1]


def _random_valid_name(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Prefer more common codes but cover the rest
    popular = {b"OK": 4, b"INVALID_ARGUMENT": 2, b"NOT_FOUND": 2, b"ALREADY_EXISTS": 2, b"UNKNOWN": 2}
    items = []
    for n in enum_names:
        items.append((popular.get(n, 1), n))
    return _weighted_choice(rng, items)


def _random_invalid_variant(rng: random.Random, base: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Create likely-to-fail variants while keeping ASCII
    ops = []
    # case flip a random segment
    def flip_case(b: bytes) -> bytes:
        s = bytearray(b)
        if not s:
            return s
        i = rng.randrange(len(s))
        c = s[i]
        if 65 <= c <= 90:
            s[i] = c + 32
        elif 97 <= c <= 122:
            s[i] = c - 32
        return bytes(s)
    ops.append(flip_case)

    # insert space or dash
    def insert_sep(b: bytes) -> bytes:
        s = bytearray(b)
        pos = rng.randrange(len(s)+1)
        s[pos:pos] = rng.choice([b" ", b"-", b"__"])  # insert one of these
        return bytes(s)
    ops.append(insert_sep)

    # add leading/trailing whitespace
    def pad_ws(b: bytes) -> bytes:
        left = rng.choice([b"", b" ", b"\t"]) if rng.random() < 0.7 else b""
        right = rng.choice([b"", b" ", b"\n"]) if rng.random() < 0.7 else b""
        return left + b + right
    ops.append(pad_ws)

    # duplicate underscore somewhere
    def dup_us(b: bytes) -> bytes:
        if b"_" not in b:
            return b + b"_"
        i = b.find(b"_")
        return b[:i] + b"__" + b[i+1:]
    ops.append(dup_us)

    fn = rng.choice(ops)
    return fn(base)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide whether to produce a valid or invalid name.
    # Bias towards valid to exercise success path often, but include failures.
    make_valid = rng.random() < 0.65

    if make_valid:
        # Choose either from the enum list directly or craft a specific interesting valid name
        s = _random_valid_name(rng)
    else:
        # Either pick a canned non-matching or derive an invalid variant from a valid base
        if rng.random() < 0.5 and non_matching:
            s = rng.choice(non_matching)
        else:
            base = _random_valid_name(rng)
            s = _random_invalid_variant(rng, base)

    # Ensure size limit and bytes type
    if len(s) > 4096:
        s = s[:4096]
    return bytes(s)
